reading.body:
ELEVATE Government Affairs filed 130 AI lobbying reports, and its largest AI client is Microsoft, with 15 filings.

The client list splits into two groups. One is technology and data companies: Microsoft, Meta Platforms, Applied Digital, Lytx, and Excella. The other is five professional sports players associations, each with 14 or 15 AI filings. That second group is the notable pattern. Sports unions are not AI developers, so their filings most likely concern the use of AI in areas like broadcasting, likeness rights, and player data, though the filings record only that AI was lobbied on, not the position taken.

The lobbyist counts show how concentrated the work is. Robert Chamberlin appears on 125 AI filings and Samuel Whitehorn on 123, out of 130 total. The remaining nine lobbyists range from 95 filings down to 2. A small team carries nearly all of this firm's AI lobbying volume.

This data covers one firm's LDA filings and nothing about outcomes. It does not show which bills were named, what the clients sought, or whether any lobbying changed a vote. It also says nothing about compute, data centers, or power, so no claim about the grid can be drawn from it.

summary: ELEVATE GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS, LLC filed 130 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 401105417.
